question: What does it cost PAL to wrongly label a booking in each of the four new segments (MICE, Ultra Wealthy Leisure, Intl. Student, Outbound International Leisure)?
blocks: The scoring stage entirely - the model is graded by an asymmetric cost matrix and the new segments have no weights
our_recommendation: This is a business input we must not invent. If you want to see the model run first, we can use the nearest existing weight as an explicit placeholder.

question: Budget/Adventure will hold 49.9% of all bookings after the change. Accept that, or split the segment?
blocks: The taxonomy change; and any targeting built on Budget/Adventure
our_recommendation: Accept for now. We ship fare tier as a reporting band (Budget 7.3M / Mid 3.5M) which gives the split without inventing a customer type. We tested a real split and it failed - the 'mid-tier traveller' turned out to be mostly people booking late, which pricing already explains.

question: Premium Bleisure shrinks 29% (481,666 to 343,100) because Ultra Wealthy Leisure takes its top end. Accept?
blocks: The taxonomy change; existing Premium Bleisure persona slides become stale
our_recommendation: Accept - it is the direct and correct consequence of approving Ultra Wealthy Leisure, which is a premium subset.

question: 21.8% of bookings change segment. When should this land?
blocks: Publication of any new segment figure; persona cards, scorecards and drift baselines all go stale the same day
our_recommendation: Land it before the next reporting cycle rather than mid-cycle, and re-run validation before publishing any new segment size.

question: A Filipino family of four flying to Japan in economy - is that Family, or Outbound International Leisure?
blocks: 190,777 bookings. Family ends at either 350,527 or 159,821
our_recommendation: Keep it in Family (what we drafted), but this is genuinely ambiguous and yours to call. Arguably Outbound should win because Family has no positive definition.

question: Does the Family segment mean anything beyond 'they booked as a group'?
blocks: 6 rules, and whether Family is an honest segment name
our_recommendation: Today Family is only 'a group booking no other rule claimed' - 100% of it. We cannot tell a family from three colleagues or a barkada. If there is no further signal, rename it Group Travel, which is all we actually measure.
answer: might be best to drop family as only other indicator would be group travel during long weekends

question: When a group books 45+ days ahead for a 3-7 night trip to a convention hub, is that MICE or Family?
blocks: 25,064 bookings that satisfy both definitions
our_recommendation: MICE should be checked first. It has a real positive definition; Family is a residual bucket.

question: Can we have FarebasisCode? (already listed in PAL's own data dictionary)
blocks: The one open confound on our strongest finding
our_recommendation: Manila-Gulf traffic shows a real one-month travel rhythm, which RM Domestic attributes to employer-mandated leave. If Gulf economy fares carry a one-month maximum-stay condition, the fare rule produces an identical pattern. We cannot separate the two without the fare basis, and the answer decides whether the rule generalises.

question: Can we have Isupgrade, IsTourCode and IsFrequentFlyer?
blocks: Independent validation of every segment boundary
our_recommendation: To measure whether our segments are right we need facts the rules never used. We are down to two such fields and the new rules spend one. All three of these are in your dictionary and no rule in the workbook touches any of them, so they are clean.

question: Can we have PNR party size (passengers per booking)? If not, can the group indicator plus a group fare class stand in?
blocks: One SME rule outright (MICE cabin rule), and it bears on the whole Family question
our_recommendation: The extract's passenger count is always 1 per sector, so 'MICE cannot be business class if party > 10' is unimplementable. RM Domestic noted this limitation themselves.

question: Can we have loyalty tier / Mabuhay status?
blocks: The Mabuhay Loyalist segment
our_recommendation: Standing request. Mabuhay is currently 0.03% of bookings - not because the segment is small but because we can only see award redemptions. The segment is real; our ability to see it is not.

question: Can you confirm the currency of the revenue fields?
blocks: Every revenue figure we quote
our_recommendation: Our own guard says the extract is plausibly single-currency (7.3x median spread across 26 issuing countries) but it has never been confirmed.

question: We narrowed your OFW rule from '[Middle East / East Asia Hubs]' to the Gulf only (DXB, RUH, DMM, DOH). Agreed?
blocks: Rule S14, 118,841 bookings
our_recommendation: Hong Kong and Taipei show the one-month pattern on only 1.9% of their round trips against 19.1% for the Gulf. Including them drops the rule's discrimination below chance (0.375 vs 0.676 Gulf-only).

question: Your route rules are written as MNLDXB, MNLRUH etc. For rules about workers coming home we read them direction-agnostically. Agreed?
blocks: The single most valuable rule in the workbook
our_recommendation: Gulf round trips start in the Gulf 260,216 times against Manila's 26,195. A worker based in Riyadh flying home is RUHMNL, not MNLRUH. Read literally your rule matched 5,166 bookings instead of 118,841 - 23x fewer. Note we kept MNL-outbound for the rule about workers leaving for the job, which is correct as written.
answer: do not agree, RUHMNL should be read as is

question: Your rule says OFWs hold '~30 or ~45 day' leave. We find the 30-night pattern strongly but no excess at 45. Do you still want 28-45 as the band?
blocks: The band on rule S14
our_recommendation: We kept 28-45 as you stated it, but flagged that only the 30 end is supported by the data.
answer: edit this rule as recommended as seen in the data

question: We dropped the academic-month clause from your Intl. Student rule, keeping only the 90-150 night stay. Agreed?
blocks: Rule S38 - now fires on 51,223 bookings instead of 17,354
our_recommendation: We are protecting departure month as an independent check on our own work. The stay length was the primary signal and stands alone; the months were a refinement.

question: Two of your 'cannot be' rules carried only moderate confidence, so we demoted them to strong tendencies rather than vetoes. Agreed?
blocks: Rules S29 and S30
our_recommendation: One would have vetoed 63% of all bookings and the other 33% of round trips, on moderate confidence. A veto that large needs to be marked certain.

question: We demoted 'Family must be a group booking' from a definitive rule to a tendency. Agreed?
blocks: 6 rules across 533,203 group bookings
our_recommendation: 'Must be' means no matter what else is true - it would have outranked Corporate, Pilgrimage and OFW, pulling 162,556 bookings into Family and growing it 44%. Your own later rules claim those same bookings for five other segments.
answer: agreed might be best to drop family as only other indicator would be group travel during long weekends

question: Your sea-crew rule requires the connecting sector to be on another airline. We cannot check that, so the rule fires wider than you intended. Acceptable?
blocks: Rule S13, 236,842 bookings
our_recommendation: The extract's operating-carrier field is constant 'PR' throughout, so the other-airline leg is unverifiable. We transcribed the rest of the condition and flagged the gap.

question: We set aside five of your rules that turn on departure month (peak season, Q4-Q1 peak, summer spike, Lent/Easter, off-peak long stays). Agreed?
blocks: 5 rules, kept in the file marked 'withdrawn' rather than deleted
our_recommendation: Same reason as C4 - we are keeping departure month as an independent check on our own segments. For these five the month was the whole claim, so nothing survives removing it. They are retained in the file so you can see exactly what we held back.

question: The Power BI wish list sheet came back with headers only. Which fields and views does each department want?
owner: All departments (RM, Sales, Marketing, CA, Loyalty, CE)
blocks: The BI half of the original ask
our_recommendation: This was half of what we sent. Worth a short form or a 20-minute call per department rather than a spreadsheet.

question: Digital Nomad - how would you identify one from anonymous booking data?
blocks: The one segment in the original requirement we have never implemented
our_recommendation: Our seeded placeholder came back untouched, still reading 'pending SME input'. We have no way to anchor this segment and would rather you define it than we guess.

question: Pilgrimage - exact religious-hub airport codes and seasonal date ranges?
blocks: 4 pilgrimage rules
our_recommendation: Partly answered by measurement, and the answer is discouraging: the Catholic hubs (Rome, Tel Aviv, Paris, Lisbon) carry only 28,224 trip endpoints against 70,650 for Jeddah/Medina, so all four of your pilgrimage rules fire on under 700 bookings each. Worth knowing before investing more in them.
answer: travel to meccah normally outbound from MNL is May and return is JUN. No other airport codes to add

question: Four segments we do model received no input at all - Mabuhay Loyalist, Family, Budget/Adventure, Digital Nomad. Can a second round cover them?
blocks: Rule coverage for 4 of our segments
our_recommendation: Twelve rules came back for three segments we did not model, and nothing for four that we do. A second round should also be domestic-focused: of the 39 rules only 1 names domestic routes, and the two fields domestic rules most need are weakest there (age is on 0.98% of domestic bookings; stay length does not exist for one-way trips).
